headline: Profit dips year over year despite sales growth, outlook up
summary_short: Carrier's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 3.9% y/y to $6.35B (4% per the release, on 3% organic growth plus FX), while diluted EPS of $0.60 fell 11.8% y/y but jumped sequentially from Q1's seasonally weak $0.28.
summary_long: Q2 net sales rose 4% y/y (3% organic, 1% FX) to $6,351M, led by CSA strength (RLC up 9-10%), partly offset by Commercial delivery timing. GAAP operating profit fell 9% y/y as favorable volume/productivity were outweighed by higher input costs and unfavorable mix; adjusted operating margin fell 190bps to 17.2%. Free cash flow was $810M on $927M of operating cash flow. Cash fell to $1,344M from $1,555M at year-end 2025; net debt rose to $10,608M from $10,278M. Carrier raised full-year guidance to ~$23B sales, ~$3.5B adjusted operating profit, and ~$2.90 adjusted EPS (from ~$22B/~$3.4B/~$2.80), citing record backlog and stronger-than-expected first-half results, while flagging a ~$0.05 adjusted-EPS drag from the NORESCO exit and new U.S. factory costs.

drivers.explanation: Organic sales +3% driven by strong CSA segment performance (Residential/Light Commercial up 9-10%), plus a 1% FX tailwind; Commercial delivery timing was a partial offset.
Adjusted operating margin fell 190bps y/y to 17.2% — volume and productivity gains were outweighed by cost inflation and an unfavorable mix shift.
GAAP EPS fell 14% y/y to $0.60, driven by lower operating profit and a higher effective tax rate, partly offset by a lower share count from buybacks.

Full-year 2026 guidance raised to ~$23B sales, ~$3.5B adjusted operating profit and ~$2.90 adjusted EPS, citing record backlog, a stronger-than-expected first half, and continued data-center-driven order strength (total orders up ~40%).
